cfg4.same_expectation_why: "Allow Access" and "GO TO SET" are both about file access, but the words are so different that I am not sure whether "GO TO SET" gives access or just takes me to another place first.
cfg4.affects_navigation: Yes; I need to know whether one press gives access or whether I will be sent into the phone's settings and have to find my way back.

first_pass.why: "Allow Access" is clear. "GO TO SET" is not a phrase I can read with certainty, so I cannot be sure the two are the same step, and I would worry I had taken a wrong turn.
first_pass.solution: Use the same plain words for the same job, for example "Allow file access" on both, and if one sends me to the phone's settings, say "Open phone settings".

test_cases.what_to_try: On the main screen press "Allow Access" and see where you land; come straight back with the phone's Back without switching anything. Then press the round black button at the lower right, and in the box press GO TO SET; see where you land, and come back with Back.
test_cases.real_if: you didn't recognise GO TO SET as the same thing as Allow Access, or weren't sure where either one took you
test_cases.not_real_if: you could tell they were the same step, and both took you where you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I did the two halves in the opposite order from the one you gave, because the permission box was already open from the scan test. First, in the "Request permission to access all files" box, I pressed GO TO SET. It took me out of the app into the phone's own page, "All files access", with the app's name and a switch, "Allow access to manage all files", which was off. I did not touch the switch, and I pressed Back. That returned me to the app's main screen, and the box had gone. Then I pressed "Allow Access" in the middle of the main screen. After a moment it took me to exactly the same phone page, "All files access", with the same switch. I pressed Back again without switching anything and was back on the main screen. So both buttons do the same thing and land in the same place. What caught me out is that neither one actually allows access. Both send me to the phone's settings, where I would have to find and flip a switch myself. "Allow Access" made me expect that pressing it would be enough. "GO TO SET" was, in the end, the more honest of the two, but I could not read it with confidence beforehand. I can now tell they are the same step. My concern moved rather than disappeared: the wording of both buttons does not prepare me for being taken out of the app into a phone settings page.
